Tables.Title: Three Validated Risk Models for Stroke
Some Best Known Published Clinical Scores With Potential Advantages

Scores.Score Components: CHF, hypertension, age (≥65 y is 1 point, ≥75 y is 2 points), diabetes, stroke/TIA (2 points)
Scores.Potential Advantages: CHADS2 was superior to existing risk classification schemes

Scores.Score Components: CHF, hypertension, age ≥75 y, diabetes, stroke/TIA, vascular disease, age 65-74 y, female sex
Scores.Potential Advantages: Most commonly used and studied successor to CHADS2

Scores.Score Components: Age (65-74 y is 3 points, 75-84 y is 6 points, ≥85 y is 6 points), hypertension, diabetes, CHF, proteinuria
Scores.Potential Advantages: Includes more age categories, renal function, and proteinuria

Scores.Score Components: Web-based, uses routinely collected clinical data, and includes a total of 16 questions
Scores.Potential Advantages: Web-based tool for predicting stroke and mortality

Scores.Score Components: Expanded lower threshold for age to 50 y (1 point for age 50-74 y)

Text Analysis: These scores are problematic to use in clinical decision-making because they incorporate several clinical factors that increase the risks of both stroke and bleeding such as age, hypertension, renal disease, and previous stroke.

Assessment of risk factors specific for bleeding may suggest interventions to reduce bleeding risk, such as discontinuing antiplatelet medications or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medications or the use of LAAO devices.
The decision to treat with OACs for stroke prevention in patients with a CHA2DS2-VASc of 1 may require additional discussion with patients.
